requested_parts: Number of Escape Pods selected in a four-player game
How selected Pods are distributed and oriented at setup
Tokens initially placed in the Intruder bag
answers.answer:
1. Select 3 Escape Pod tokens for four players.
2. Place the lowest-numbered Pod in Section A, the next numbered Pod in Section B, and continue alternating A/B in numerical order. All selected Pods start Locked side up.
3. The bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, and 1 additional Adult per player. With four players that is 7 Adults total.
answers.evidence:
1. “Take randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens: 2 pods for 1–2 players, 3 for 3–4 players, 4 for 5 players.”
2. “Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section ‘A’, the next (in numerical order) in Section ‘B’, then alternate A/B. All pods start with their Locked side face up. Return the rest to the box.”
3. “Put these Intruder tokens in the Intruder bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player.” Inference: four players means 3 + 4 = 7 Adults in the bag.

requested_parts: How Objective cards are filtered and dealt
When each player chooses which Objective to keep
What happens to the rejected Objective
Whether Eggs trigger the Objective choice
answers.answer:
1. Remove from each (Corporate and Personal) Objective deck every card that requires more players than are in the game; shuffle the decks separately and deal each player one from each deck, kept hidden.
2. Each player chooses one of their two cards at the First Encounter: the first time an Intruder miniature appears on the board.
3. Remove the unchosen Objective from the game face down, unseen by anyone. Players may never look at other players’ removed Objectives.
4. No. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this choice.
answers.evidence:
1. “Let P be the actual number of players in this game. Remove from both Objective decks (Corporate and Personal) every card requiring more than P players. Shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card, kept hidden.”
2–4. “First Encounter: the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others’ removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.”

requested_parts: What is discarded to pay for an Action card printed cost 2 when that card is held along with two other Action cards and two Contamination cards
Whether Contamination cards can pay the cost
How to resolve a card offering OR effects
answers.answer:
1. Discard the played Action card plus two other Action cards, for three Action cards total. The two Contamination cards are not discarded to pay.
2. Contamination cards cannot substitute for Action cards in any Action cost.
3. If the Action card has sections separated by OR, choose one of the sections/effects.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total.” “Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost.” For cost 2, inference from that rule: discard the played card and 2 additional Action cards, 3 total; neither Contamination card pays.
3. “If a card has two sections separated by ‘OR,’ choose one.”

requested_parts: When Fire damage is taken by a Character who takes one Action and passes in a burning Room
Whether they can take another Action during this Player Phase
Whether they can discard cards after passing
Whether later players’ rounds cause more Fire damage to them that turn
answers.answer:
1. The Character takes 1 Light Wound at the end of their passing round, after declaring Pass.
2. No. After passing they sit out normal rounds for the rest of the Player Phase.
3. They do not take another ordinary Action or discard cards to pay for one after passing; the cited post-pass allowance is only an Interruption, and it is permitted only if they are in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action.
4. No. Later players’ rounds do not give that Character further Fire wounds that turn.
answers.evidence:
1, 4. “Fire in your Room | Take 1 Light Wound at the end of your own passing round. Later players’ rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn.” “Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.”
2. “I. Player Phase: … rounds of 2 Actions (or 1 Action + pass, or pass) clockwise until all players pass — after passing you sit out normal rounds for the rest of the Phase (Interruption remains permitted).”
3. Inference from the Player Phase rule that passing sits the Character out of normal rounds: they have no further ordinary Action to pay for or discard cards for. The summary specifies the exception: “Interruption may still be played after passing, but it requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere.”

requested_parts: What happens when entering an empty unexplored Room: tile and Item Counter
How the Exploration effect resolves
When the Noise roll occurs and where the resulting token/marker goes
How Silence alters the Noise roll
How Danger alters the Noise roll
How an already occupied destination alters the Noise roll
answers.answer:
1. Flip the unexplored Room tile face up, reveal its Exploration token, and set the Item Counter to the number shown on the token (except the Nest and Room Covered With Slime, which have no Item count).
2. Resolve the Exploration effect and then remove that token from the game. Silence or Danger replaces the ordinary Movement Noise roll; resolve that result without rolling again.
3. If the result is not Silence or Danger and the destination is empty, roll Noise. On a 1–4 put a Noise marker in the correspondingly numbered Corridor connected to the entered Room (including Technical Corridors where applicable); if that Corridor already has a marker, resolve an Encounter instead. A Noise roll result of Danger moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room, or, if none are eligible, places markers in every connected Corridor lacking one. Silence places no marker.
4. Silence means no Movement Noise roll and nothing happens, unless the Character has Slime, in which case Silence resolves as Danger.
5. Danger means no Movement Noise roll: move all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the entered Room. If no eligible Intruders exist, place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor without one.
6. If a Character or Intruder is already in the destination, do not roll Movement Noise. (A Silence/Danger Exploration result is resolved as stated and itself does not call for a Noise roll.)
answers.evidence:
1–2. “After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule. A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward.” “Item Counter: the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token’s number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot.”
3–5. “Result 1, 2, 3, or 4: place a Noise marker in the Corridor with that number connected to the Room you entered (counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” “Danger: if there is an Intruder in a neighboring Room (and it is not in Combat with any Character), move it into this Room — all eligible Intruders move. If there are no Intruders in neighboring Rooms (or they are in Combat), place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor that lacks one (counting Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance).” “Silence: nothing happens; no marker. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve ‘Danger’ instead.”
6. “Remember: never roll for Noise when moving into a Room containing another Character or an Intruder.”

requested_parts: Careful Movement cost and what it replaces
When Careful Movement is forbidden
Whether a Closed Door can be crossed
Whether a miniature can stop in a Corridor
answers.answer:
1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. After entering the destination, instead of rolling Noise, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to that Room. It also replaces an automatic Silence or Danger Exploration result with that chosen Noise placement.
2. It is forbidden in Combat and if every Corridor connected to the destination already has a Noise marker.
3. No. Normal Movement restrictions apply, and a Closed Door blocks passage.
4. No. Characters and Intruders may occupy Rooms only and may never stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence:
1–3. “Careful Movement (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. The FAQ clarifies that Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement.”
4. “Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor.”

requested_parts: Encounter sequence caused by rolling a number for a Corridor that already has Noise
What happens to Noise
Where the drawn token goes
How Surprise Attack is determined
Whether Contamination cards count in that comparison
answers.answer:
1. Since that Corridor already has a Noise marker, resolve an Encounter. First discard all Noise markers in every Corridor connected to the Room (including connected Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance); draw one Intruder token; place its matching miniature if it is not Blank; then compare the drawn token’s number with the triggering player’s hand.
2. The connected Noise markers are discarded at the start of the Encounter. If the bag draw is Blank, instead put a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to the Room; the Encounter ends without an Intruder appearing, and return the Blank token to the bag.
3. Keep a drawn non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank is returned to the bag after its procedure.
4. If the triggering player has fewer cards than the number on the non-Blank token, the appearing Intruder makes a Surprise Attack against that Character; equal or more means no Surprise Attack.
5. Yes. Both Action and Contamination cards in the triggering player’s hand count.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” “Resolve: 1. Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance). 2. Draw 1 Intruder token from the bag (symbol on one side, number on the other). Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank follows its separate return procedure. 3. Place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room. 4. Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack (an Intruder Attack against that Character). Equal or more → nothing happens.”
3–5. “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” The quoted Encounter rule explicitly includes Contamination in the comparison and gives the non-Blank token destination.

requested_parts: How Danger resolves with several eligible neighboring Intruders
What Danger does when no Intruders are eligible
Whether an Intruder moving into your Room counts as an Encounter
How Slime affects Silence
answers.answer:
1. All eligible Intruders in neighboring Rooms move into the Room; eligibility excludes an Intruder in Combat with any Character.
2. If there are no eligible neighboring Intruders (including when neighboring Intruders are in Combat), place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor that does not already have one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.
3. No. An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is not an Encounter; they are simply in Combat.
4. While the Character has Slime, every Silence result on a Noise roll or Exploration token resolves as Danger.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.”
3. “An Encounter is any instance of an Intruder appearing (via an Intruder-bag draw) in a Room where a Character is present. Some Event cards (e.g., Hatching) and Intruder Attack cards can also trigger Encounters. An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter (they are simply in Combat).”
4. “while on your board, every ‘Silence’ result (Noise roll or Exploration token) becomes ‘Danger.’”

requested_parts: What happens to Noise and the Blank during a Blank Encounter draw
Whether an Adult is added in an Encounter with Blank
What happens to Blank during bag development
answers.answer:
1. For a Blank drawn during an Encounter, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to that Room, return the Blank to the bag, and end the Encounter without a miniature appearing. The opening Encounter step has already discarded all Noise markers from all connected Corridors.
2. Add an Adult token to the bag only if the Blank was the last token in the bag; if no Adult is available, nothing is added.
3. During bag development, Blank adds 1 Adult token to the bag if one is available, then returns to the bag; if none is available, no Adult is added.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” The Encounter sequence also says: “Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance).”
3. “Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag.”

requested_parts: Where two Intruders attempting together to cross one Closed Door end
What happens to the Door
Whether it can later close
Whether a Noise-triggered appearance is blocked by the Closed Door
answers.answer:
1. Both Intruders stay in the Room they were trying to leave; neither crosses the Closed Door.
2. The Intruders destroy the Door.
3. A Destroyed Door allows movement through it and only the Plasma Torch Item can close it again.
4. No. If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.
answers.evidence:
1–2. “Closed = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put).”
3–4. “Destroyed = lying token: movement allowed; only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it.” “If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.”
